lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: We don't do names up here and we don't do headcounts. You can eat, you can sleep, you can stay the winter. If you're counting anybody, you can leave, and I'll not be rude about it.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Forty of us. Was eleven when I came up. People walk out of Halden with nothing and they get as far as the third terrace before they stop flinching at movement, and that's usually about four days.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: There's an old woman in the founding charter who kept this place common instead of endowed. Turned down money, when they had nothing. Whoever she was, she's the reason there's a gate here with nobody standing on it.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Endowed land, this. There's a trust, and a wall, and a list of who's entitled to be inside it. We're on the list. Plenty of people aren't, and they can see the wall from where they're standing.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: There's a vote this week, down there. Won't change anything up here. That's rather the point of up here, and if it ever stops being true we'll have a problem I don't know how to solve.

lines.speaker: commune_speaker
lines.text: Word came up that somebody got a clause into the Handover. Forty people cheered at a treaty amendment. I have been up this mountain nineteen years and I have never seen that happen.
